ai.title: CAO 9-2020: Clearance Procedures sa Formal Entry
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang CAO 9-2020 ang nagtatakda ng buong proseso ng customs clearance para sa goods na entered for consumption sa Formal Entry Process, mula declaration hanggang release.

🔍 Breakdown: Sec. 1-2 Scope at Objective; Sec. 3 Definitions; Sec. 4 General Provisions (entry, owner, liability, documents, valuation methods, classification, rates); Sec. 5 Lodgement; Sec. 6 Examination; Sec. 7 Assessment; Sec. 8 Payment; Sec. 9 Release; Sec. 10-11 Disputes at Alert Orders; Sec. 12-17 Penal, Transitory, Review, Repealing, Separability, Effectivity.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Isipin mo ang shipment mo bilang may 'journey': mag-lodge ng declaration, ma-examine kung kailangan, ma-assess, bayaran, tapos ma-release. Lahat ng hakbang na iyan ay dito nakasulat.

📦 Halimbawa: Nag-import ng electronics na FOB Php200,000. Nag-lodge ang broker sa loob ng 15 araw, napili for physical examination, na-assess ng FAN, nabayaran sa AAB at na-release via OLRS.

⭐ Bakit Mahalaga Ito? Ito ang pangunahing guide ng broker at importer sa pang-araw-araw na clearance, at madalas itong lumalabas sa Customs Broker board exam.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: 15 calendar days para mag-lodge; Php50,000 FOB/FCA threshold para sa Formal Entry; 45 + 45 days sa provisional declaration; 20% per annum legal interest; 3 years period of limitation.

🎯 Board Exam Tip: Memorize ang six valuation methods in order, ang GRI Rules 1 to 6, at ang mga deadline at period (15, 45, 7 working days, 3 years).

❓ Madalas Malito ang Students: Pareho ba ang Alert Order at pre-lodgement control? Hindi; ang Alert Order ay inilalabas pagkatapos mag-lodge at bago ang release, samantalang ang pre-lodgement control ay bago pa mag-lodge.

🔗 Related Topics: CMTA, CAO 2-2020 (Dispute Settlement and Protest), CAO 7-2019 (Alert Order), CAO 5-2019 (Customs Broker), GATT Valuation Agreement, Revised Kyoto Convention.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Tandaan ang Titles na sakop (I, IV, VII, XV, XVI); ito ang basehan ng buong procedure.

paragraphs.text: This CAO shall apply to all importations entered for consumption through a Formal Entry Process, whether or not subject to payment of duties and taxes.

ai.title: Scope
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sakop ng CAO ang lahat ng importation na entered for consumption sa pamamagitan ng Formal Entry Process.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kahit duty-free pa ang shipment, basta Formal Entry at pang-consumption, sakop pa rin ito ng CAO.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hindi hadlang sa coverage kung may binabayarang duties at taxes o wala.

paragraphs.text: To prescribe the procedures in the customs clearance of imports covered by goods declaration for consumption through a Formal Entry Process, that are aligned with international standards and best practices.

ai.title: Objective
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Layunin nitong magtakda ng clearance procedures para sa Formal Entry na naka-align sa international standards.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Isang malinaw na proseso mula lodgement hanggang release na sumusunod sa best practices tulad ng Revised Kyoto Convention.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Keywords na madalas lumabas sa exam: 'international standards and best practices'.

paragraphs.text: Air Waybill (AWB) — shall refer to a transport document for airfreight used by airlines and international freight forwarders which specifies the holder or consignee of the bill who has the right to claim delivery of the goods when they arrive at the port of destination. It is a contract of carriage that includes carrier conditions, such as limits of liability and claims procedures. In addition, it contains transport instructions to airlines and carriers, a description of the goods, and applicable transportation charges.

ai.title: Air Waybill (AWB)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Transport document ng airfreight na nagsasabi kung sino ang may karapatang mag-claim ng goods.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'kontrata at resibo' ng air cargo; proof na ikaw ang puwedeng kumuha ng shipment sa airport.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: AWB ay para sa air; BL ay para sa sea.

paragraphs.text: Alert Order — shall refer to a written Order issued by the Commissioner, District Collector, or other customs officers authorized in writing by the Commissioner after the Lodgement of Goods Declaration and before their actual release from customs custody, on the basis of Derogatory Information regarding possible non-compliance with the CMTA and other laws, rules and regulations enforced by Customs.

ai.content:

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang 'hold' sa shipment kapag may hinala ng non-compliance.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Alert Order ay AFTER lodgement; ang pre-lodgement control ay BEFORE.

paragraphs.text: Bill of Lading (BL) — shall refer to a transport document issued by shipping lines, carriers and international freight forwarders or non-vessel operating common carrier for water-borne freight. The holder or consignee of the bill has the right to claim delivery of the goods at the port of destination. It is a contract of carriage that includes carrier conditions, such as limits of liability and claims procedures. In addition, it contains transport instructions to shipping lines and carriers, a description of the goods, and applicable transportation charges.

paragraphs.text: Break Bulk Cargo — shall refer to non-containerized general cargo stored in boxes, bales, pallets or other individual units to be loaded onto or discharged from vessels, not shipped in containers or in bulk.

paragraphs.text: Clearance — shall refer to the completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption.

ai.content:

paragraphs.text: Commercial Quantity — shall refer to the quantity for a given kind or class of articles which are in excess of what is compatible with or commensurate with a person's normal requirements for personal use.

paragraphs.text: Conditionally Tax and/or Duty-Exempt Importation — shall refer to goods exempt from the payment of import duties and/or taxes upon compliance with certain formalities prescribed under pertinent customs issuances.

paragraphs.text: Customs Broker — shall refer to any person who is a bona fide holder of a valid Certificate of Registration or Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulatory Board and Professional Regulation Commission pursuant to Republic Act No. 9280, as amended, otherwise known as the “Customs Brokers Act of 2004”, as further amended by Republic Act No. 9853. paragraphs.text: Declarant — shall refer to any person who makes a goods declaration or in whose name a goods declaration is made, as enumerated under Section 5.1 of this CAO. Further, in the processing of goods declaration under the Formal Entry Process, the declarant must be accredited and registered with the Bureau and authorized to electronically lodge the goods declaration.

paragraphs.text: Electronic Inward Foreign Cargo Manifest (e-IFCM) — shall refer to the advance electronic conveyance of freight information to the Bureau prior to the arrival of the shipment at the port of entry and provides the detailed list of cargo (freight) on board a vessel or aircraft giving the commercial particulars of the goods, such as transport document numbers, consignors, consignees, marks and numbers, number and kind of packages, weight, descriptions, quantities of the goods and destination.

paragraphs.text: Examination of Goods — shall refer to the physical, documentary, or non-intrusive inspection of goods to ensure that the nature, origin, condition, quantity, value and tariff classification of the goods are in accordance with the particulars furnished in the goods declaration and other supporting documents.

ai.content:

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Chine-check kung totoo ang nakasulat sa declaration.

paragraphs.text: Formal Entry Process — shall refer to the cargo clearance process for imported shipments considered to be of commercial nature which are those in excess of FOB or FCA value limitation for informal entry and those for which the informal entry process may not be used, subject to the exceptions provided under the CMTA.

ai.title: Formal Entry Process
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Clearance process para sa commercial shipments na lampas sa informal entry limit.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kapag malaki ang value o hindi puwede ang informal, Formal Entry ang gagamitin.
